title: Case study
summary: A composite of the route that works: second-year, non-target, no internship, summer offer.

blocks.md:
*The details below are a composite drawn from several students' journeys, not one person.*

**Starting point (June, end of first year).** Economics at a university outside the usual list. First-year average 66. One summer job in retail. No spring week — she applied to two in October of first year, late, and heard nothing.

**Summer.** Built the CV in the four-section format. Started a three-statement model of a listed UK grocer, working from the annual report; it took five weekends and taught her more accounting than the module had. Sent 40 LinkedIn notes to analysts from her university and city; 11 replied; 7 calls.

**September.** Applied to 12 summer analyst programmes in the first week each opened, plus three off-cycles at European banks. One of the seven analysts she had spoken to, at a mid-market bank, offered to flag her application without being asked.

**October – November.** Four first-round interviews: two bulge bracket, one mid-market, one boutique. The mid-market interviewer asked her to walk through a £10m depreciation increase; she gave the canonical answer in 40 seconds and then explained the deferred-tax wrinkle he had not asked about. He later said that was the moment.

**December.** Superday at the mid-market bank: two technical rounds, one fit, one case. The model on her laptop came up in the fit round when asked what she had done to prepare; she opened it. Offer the following week.

**What generalised.** Applying early. Manufacturing one piece of hard evidence. Turning networking into a process with a spreadsheet. Knowing the canonical answers cold, and the trap under each one.
